clue.text: Everything this pop musician does is a hit

definitions.text: Everything this pop musician does is a hit

parts.words: Everything this pop musician does is a hit
parts.note: read literally, a player whose every action is striking something: the band member on sticks and skins

explanation.surface: A praise-singer claims a pop star has never had a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' pretends to mean a chart success; literally, this musician spends the whole gig hitting things.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist in a band strikes the kit with sticks throughout every song.

clue.text: Flags love to be in some rain

indicators.note: the word for love is told to sit within the letters for some rain

parts.note: a few drops of rain
love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Bunting gets a soaking during a light shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like a noun (banners) but is the verb: wilts.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or sag, the same as wilting downward.

clue.text: Release bolt? No luck?

indicators.note: to bolt is to run off wildly, so the letters of No luck scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to open a door, but the bolt won't budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' looks like part of the definition (release a bolt) but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something held fast, such as a door, is to open its fastening.

clue.text: Time in history that saw Islam edged out?

definitions.text: Time in history that saw Islam edged out?

parts.words: Time in history that saw Islam edged out?
parts.note: the medieval era saw Moors pushed out of Spain; playfully, the word Islam with its edges out leaves only its central letters, its middle

explanation.surface: A history question about a period when Muslim power was pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the edges from ISLAM and what remains is its middle: a cryptic hint at the era's name, hung on the Reconquista.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval period, roughly 500 to 1500 AD, sits between antiquity and the modern era.

clue.text: Steal books to build automaton

parts.note: to steal is to rob
OT, the Old Testament, is the usual crossword abbreviation for a set of books

explanation.surface: A thief pinches library books to build a mechanical man.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical device that acts by itself, often humanoid, is a machine of this kind.

clue.text: Given power, woman showed signs of injury

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name, a crossword favourite
a wound shows by bleeding

explanation.surface: An empowered woman is nonetheless left bruised and bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To be empowered is to be made able to act.

clue.text: Great joy seizes British plant

indicators.note: the word for great joy grips the abbreviation for British inside it

parts.note: elation, intense happiness

explanation.surface: A gardener is thrilled to grab a native specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurge genus, with milky sap, includes the poinsettia.

clue.text: A team's the centre of revolution

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A side boasts that it is the beating heart of an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests political upheaval; here it is rotation, and the centre is the line something spins round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating body turns about a straight line, its pivot line.

clue.text: There was a young lady from, for example, somewhere in Ireland

definitions.text: There was a young lady from, for example
definitions.meaning: a typical opening line of a comic five-line verse
a city and county in the Republic of Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: The comic five-line verse form takes its name from the Irish city and county.

clue.text: Yorkshire folk need alms desperately

indicators.note: desperately suggests frantic disorder, so the letters of need alms are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: People in a northern county are begging for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are upland valleys in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of the Yorkshire Dales valleys are known by this name.

clue.text: Nothing I took charge of was made smooth

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
to lead is to take charge; past tense

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they ran a smoothing operation over zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying lubricant makes a surface or mechanism run slickly.

clue.text: Psalm a bit rocky in such a church service?

definitions.note: an adjective: describing the rite of christening

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaky, so the letters of Psalm a bit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hymn goes a little wobbly during a christening service.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: the answer describes the font-and-water rite, with 'such a' pointing at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the Christian rite of washing or sprinkling with water at initiation.

clue.text: Rumours a head will roll for this embezzlement

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for rumours is lopped off, as a head rolls

parts.note: gossip and guesswork, unfounded talk

explanation.surface: Gossip suggests someone will be sacked over fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head will roll' reads as dismissal; it removes the first letter, S, from SPECULATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean misappropriating funds entrusted to one, especially public money.

clue.text: War god viewed in fear, essentially

indicators.note: the god can be seen inside the run of letters across fear essentially

explanation.surface: A deity of battle is seen as the essence of terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' pretends to mean 'at heart'; it is simply letters for the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of battle, counterpart of the Roman Mars.

clue.text: Many a contributing cause, including drink, makes a criminal

indicators.note: the first pieces take the word for drink inside them

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
a factor is something that contributes to a result
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Drinking, among many causes, turns someone to crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or offender, especially one who breaks the law.

clue.text: Central beach may offer complete freedom

indicators.note: the letters of Central beach may be rearranged to offer something new

explanation.surface: A beach in the middle of town lets you do as you please.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means literally a blank card, a signed sheet left for the holder to fill in.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlimited authority to act as one wishes, from a blank signed paper.

clue.text: Try to land

definitions.meaning: in rugby, a score made by grounding the ball over the line
of an aircraft, to arrive on the ground

explanation.definitionFit: In American football the score is grounding the ball like a rugby try; aircraft also settle on runways this way.

clue.text: Shows nervousness when involved with sect

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of with sect are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone gets jumpy when getting mixed up with a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Small involuntary jerks and tics betray anxiety.

clue.text: Those buzzing around may get stuck into this

definitions.text: Those buzzing around may get stuck into this

parts.words: Those buzzing around may get stuck into this
parts.note: insects buzzing about end up glued to a sticky hanging strip

explanation.surface: Busy people around the office may get their teeth into a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get stuck into' reads as 'tackle eagerly'; literally the buzzing insects get glued on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky strip hung up to trap insects.

clue.text: Properly brought up, learning the oil industry?

definitions.meaning: having had a good upbringing and schooling
playfully, schooled in drilling boreholes for oil

explanation.definitionFit: Being schooled thoroughly; jokingly, taught about oil boreholes.

clue.text: Draw in smoke, in healthy combination

parts.note: hale means strong and well, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Breathing smoke is somehow combined with keeping fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe air or fumes down into the lungs.

clue.text: Young bird gets ring, we hear

indicators.note: the clue says the next word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a signet is a ring bearing a seal

explanation.surface: A fledgling is given a ring, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan chicks have this special name, as a kid is a young goat; the word also sounds like a seal ring.

clue.text: Spat out "Lights out"

indicators.note: out means put into disorder, so the letters of Spat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone angrily blurts an order to switch off the lights.
explanation.walkthrough: In US military use, the bugle call for lights-out at night is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle call sounded at night signalling bedtime in camp.

clue.text: Pal I involved in risky ministerial post

indicators.note: the mixed letters go inside the word for risky

parts.note: chancy means uncertain or hazardous

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of Pal I are mixed up

explanation.surface: A friend confesses getting mixed up in a dangerous government job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns PAL into PLA; with I beside it, 'in' places the lot after CHA within the word for risky. 'ministerial' points to clergy, not government.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of a cleric attached to an institution such as a hospital or regiment.

clue.text: Face value put on one's capital

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: par is the nominal or face value of a share
one is the Roman numeral I, plus S for the possessive

explanation.surface: A face value is set on someone's capital investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, given 'face value'; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital city.

clue.text: One could be fired, disposing of a body

definitions.text: One could be fired, disposing of a body

parts.words: One could be fired, disposing of a body
parts.note: a heap of wood set alight for a cremation

explanation.surface: An employee might be sacked for getting rid of a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests dismissal; here it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of wood for burning a corpse at a funeral.

clue.text: Satisfied with occasion for local bargain

parts.note: contented, pleased
a particular time, an hour of the day

explanation.surface: Someone is content with a time for cheap pub drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub; the bargain is cut-price drinks at set times.
explanation.definitionFit: A period when a pub sells drinks at reduced prices.

clue.text: Take pictures round to popular coach

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for pictures is read backwards

parts.note: art means paintings and pictures
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A photographer snaps a well-liked bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' reads as a bus but is the verb: instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to instruct or prepare someone for a skill.

clue.text: Cutter to make rapid progress

definitions.meaning: a medical person who operates with a scalpel
split as two words, to push forward strongly

explanation.definitionFit: An operating doctor cuts with a scalpel; split in two, the letters mean press forward quickly.

clue.text: Eve's tempter repents after fall

indicators.note: a fall jumbles things, so the letters of repents are rearranged

explanation.surface: In Eden, the tempter is sorry after the Fall of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' evokes the biblical Fall; here it signals the letters tumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis a snake persuades Eve to eat the forbidden fruit.
